Under the existing EHCP framework, the appeal rights are limited to specific decisions, as outlined in section 51 of the Education and Health and Care: Plans, Compensations and Reviews (England) Act 2014. These include decisions regarding EHC needs assessments, EHC plans, and certain aspects of those plans. The appeals are subject to section 55, which mandates mediation before a child's parent or young person can appeal to the First-tier Tribunal.

Individual Support Plans (ISPs) are proposed to be developed by schools and colleges for children with Special Educational Needs (SEND), but they are not subject to independent legal appeal. This means parents and young people will not have a legal route to challenge a school if a child is not receiving the right support, as mentioned in the Hansard contribution by Nadia Whittome.

[ISP] provides more details on the development of ISPs, which will be tailored to the layers of support and include information about the child or young person's identified barriers to learning, provision, reasonable adjustments, and intended outcomes. These plans will be standardised across settings to facilitate transitions and will be used to communicate provision to parents and document actions taken between them and educators. [end of text]
